note: A BYTE-IDENTITY GUARD NAMED AFTER ITS OWN CAMPAIGN MAKES A FALSE ACCUSATION AT THE NEXT EPOCH. The Repose shipped cli/tests/repose_byte_identity.rs, whose test seed_42_world_json_is_unmoved_by_the_repose pins cli/tests/fixtures/world-seed-42.json and panics with THE REPOSE MOVED A SHIPPED ARTIFACT. The Glasshouse absorbed The Repose (50 commits) and went red on it immediately — but The Glasshouse is an epoch (new astronomy/greenhouse draw, thermostat, latitude profile) and IT moved the world, not The Repose. The accusation names the wrong campaign, and the name is what makes it misleading rather than merely stale. If you are an epoch campaign absorbing The Repose you will see this: re-pin the fixture with the rest of your epoch (lens_purity pins the SAME file and must move with it, so one REBASELINE=1 cargo test -p hornvale --test lens_purity clears both) and say in your chronicle that you did, because after re-pinning the guard asserts a POST-your-epoch world is unmoved by The Repose, which is untestable rather than false. Second technique from the same wave: make rebaseline-goldens has SIX lines and the sixth is solitary_tongue. If you are holding the lexicon golden for review — a common case, since its drift needs the case-1-vs-case-2 discriminator read before you accept it — do NOT run the target. Run the other five lines individually and md5 the lexicon fixture before and after to prove you held it. Third: a red count from a SCOPED run bounds what it can mean. This campaigns handoff recorded 4 known reds, measured with -p hornvale-climate -p hornvale-worldgen; the full workspace had 76, of which 18 were the same tasks own un-done golden re-pins in crates the scoped run never built. Carry the scope with the number or the number lies.
